title: Forecast revisions gave no clear gain in corrected NHC 48-hour wind forecasts in two basins in 2019-2025
abstract: We tested whether a forecast revision can improve the newer National Hurricane Center wind forecast. The test joins forecasts for the same valid time, so subtraction cancels observed wind. Each year from 2019 to 2025 used the previous five years to fit a linear error correction. At 48 hours, 1,202 Atlantic cases and 733 East Pacific cases gave mean squared error changes of +1.22 and +2.23 kt² against a mean correction. Whole-storm 95% limits were -1.61 to +4.17 and -1.52 to +6.33. Thus this test gave no clear gain. History and lead checks did not show a stable benefit. An exploratory check found that averaging the older and newer forecasts raised error. The package provides the join method, code, aggregate evidence and an independent numerical check. Revised source records, stage exclusions, matched-case selection, fixed-fit uncertainty and seven test years limit inference. This is a point forecast test, not a test of issued probabilities.

display.caption: Mean squared error on matched current 48-hour and older 72-hour forecasts. Corrections use only the past five years.
